business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Islamic Sharia as a Source of Legislation per Article 2 of the Constitution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (1986, in force 1992)
EU-Egypt Association Agreement (2004) including investment and services provisions
Agreement Establishing the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA, 1993)
Greater Arab Free Trade Area Agreement (GAFTA) and Unified Agreement for Investment in the Arab Countries

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 8 of 2016) and its Executive Regulations; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Rules and directives of the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU); Company Law No. 194 of 2020 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 2021) mandating UBO identification, documentation, and annual updating obligations at the General Authority for Investment (GAFI); Egypt's terrorist listing regime under Counter-Terrorism Law No. 8 of 2015 and Cabinet Decree No. 1647 of 2017 as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of Incorporation of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registrar in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Attestation Department and the Egyptian embassy or consulate in the country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn UBO declaration (electronic UBO Form) with organizational structure chart traced to natural persons
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each UBO and the authorized Egyptian incorporation agent before a Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and, for foreign UBOs, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Consular Legalization for foreign signatories

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory name and identity-based screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Egypt's domestic terrorist list (Cabinet Decree No. 1647 of 2017 as amended) prior to registration; Politically Exposed Persons as defined in Law No. 80 of 2002 require Enhanced Due Diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior-management approval in accordance with EMLCU directives, consistent with FATF Recommendations 10 and 24.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI 'Invest in Egypt' one-stop-shop incorporation portal and the Commercial Registry (Al-Shahr Al-Tijari) of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be formed in Modern Standard Arabic and registered first with GAFI; a Latin-alphabet transliteration is permitted only as a non-statutory commercial alias. The name must not duplicate or be confusingly similar to an existing registered name, must not contain misleading indications, and must pass the Commercial Registry trademark-conflict screening. The English alias cannot be used as the sole registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Financial / Malya (when implying CBE- or FRA-regulated activity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its licensed Egyptian attorney must file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Commercial Registry Committee within 15 business days of the electronic rejection notice, attaching the Arabic name rationale, a negative trademark clearance report, and any ministerial approvals obtained for sensitive tokens; if the Committee upholds the rejection, a further administrative appeal lies with the Ministry of Trade and Industry Competence Committee, and judicial nullification may be sought before the Administrative Court (State Council) within 30 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Rejected for the statutory seat of an LLC operating in this financing industry: the Commercial Registry requires a physically leased address in Egypt, and the financial-services-adjacent classification implies an expectation of on-site records, compliance files, and accounting systems. A virtual office may be used only as a supplementary correspondence address after the physical registered office is established and inspected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High (estimated 55-65% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Egyptian Tax Authority or the Social Insurance Inspector within the first 24 months of operation given the NAICS 525990 / ISIC 6499 financial-intermediation-adjacent classification).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egypt Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, particularly LLC provisions (Articles 203–231); Law on Investment No. 72 of 2017; Executive Regulations of Companies Law; Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976; Notary Public Law No. 68 of 1947.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration and One-Stop Shop; Commercial Registry under Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association (Statute) of the limited liability company, filed electronically through GAFI's one-stop shop with the Commercial Registry statement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital, but share nominal value must be at least EGP 0.05; full capital must be subscribed at incorporation and at least 50% of each quota's nominal value paid in cash at formation, with the balance payable within five years. Cash contributions are evidenced by a bank certificate; in-kind contributions require an expert valuation. No escrow account is statutorily required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company adopts in full the Articles of Association as incorporated under Law 159 of 1981; that the subscribers listed in the incorporation file are allotted their respective membership quotas; that the registered office in Egypt is designated as [address to be registered] and the manager/legal representative for process service is appointed; that [Name1] be and is hereby appointed Managing Director and [Name2] Chief Financial Officer, each to act within the powers in the Articles; and that the Managing Director is authorised to complete all statutory filings, open bank accounts, and pay incorporation fees. Resolutions adopted on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name and Verify the Corporate Object
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI electronic establishment portal under the Ministry of Investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Arabic/Latin company name, commercial registry risk search request, and the exact corporate object. The application is screened against conflicting names, trademarks, and prohibited activities. The statutory object must specifically describe non-banking revenue-based royalty financing and treasury management.
required_dossiers: Primary and secondary proposed company names
Passport, national ID or residence copy of each founder
Power of attorney if a founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, select an alternative name and resubmit online, or file a written grievance with GAFI's name-review committee; resolve conflicting trademark claims before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize the Articles of Association and Execute Subscription Undertaking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public (Cairo or governorate notary office) and legalizing GAFI officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic Articles of Association including corporate purpose, capital, quotas, management, dispute resolution, and dissolution terms. All founding shareholders must sign before the notary public; the notary authenticates signatures, pagination, and date. In-kind contributions must be value-assessed by an accredited expert before execution.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit or expert valuation of in-kind contribution
Lease/ownership evidence of intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any notary query by amending the Articles, reprinting the Arabic paginated copy, and re-signing before the notary; no new name screening is needed unless the corporate name changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application with GAFI and Obtain Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop coupled with Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized Articles through the GAFI portal, attach the address declaration and director consent forms, pay the official electronic fee schedule, and submit the integrated application. GAFI issues the incorporation certificate and creates the Commercial Register entry in coordination with the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Contract or title deed for the registered office
Consent of appointed managers and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to GAFI/Commercial Registry deficiency notice within the statutory deadline by uploading the missing documents; if rejection is based on legal form incompatibility, amend the Articles and re-execute notarization; grievance available under the Companies Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Tax Card and Tax Registration with the Egyptian Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Taxpayer Services Unit of the governing governorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, submit the tax card application, register for income tax and documentary stamp tax, and assess VAT registration threshold. The ETA issues the Tax Card showing the company's economic activity code and registered address.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association and ID/CPR of legal representative
Proof of office address (utility bill or lease)
Board resolution appointing the tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA queries the address or activity classification, provide a revised lease certificate or amend the object; any tax assessment may be objected to under the Tax Procedures Law No. 206/2020 grievance procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company and Employees with Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) – insurance office for the company's registered governorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the social insurance registration forms and obtain an NOSI insurance registration number for the company as an employer. All employees and any working managers must be registered and monthly contribution records established.
required_dossiers: List of employees and national IDs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any discrepancies in worker names, contribution category, or start dates and re-submit within 15 days; issue a grievance through NOSI appeals office for disputed contribution classifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Civil Defense Fire Safety Clearance and Workplace Occupational Safety Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Civil Defense Directorate and Ministry of Manpower occupational safety unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Inspect the leased office premises, install rated fire extinguishers and emergency exit signs, and obtain Civil Defense certificate. Register the company's workplace safety file with the Ministry of Manpower and complete the annual occupational health record.
required_dossiers: Workplace safety manual and assigned safety officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate any Civil Defense inspection findings (exit width, extinguisher accessibility, electrical load) and schedule a reinspection; provide employee medical certificates for occupational safety clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Industrial Development (GAID) – not engaged because the Fund will not own or operate an industrial facility
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operation license is required for the royalty-financing fund; the Commercial Registration, Tax Card, and Civil Defense certificate collectively constitute the administrative license for the office treasury function

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) under Law No. 4/1994 as amended by Law 9/2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening/Registration only (Category B administrative office) – no full EIA report required for a non-industrial fund management office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, process discharge, or VOC emission thresholds apply to the licensed office use; if the premises later includes DG or storage, EEAA thresholds under Executive Regulations 87/2005 (wastewater) and Law 4/1994 air-quality limits shall apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense fire safety certificate required; structural load inspection certificate for office occupancy; Ministry of Manpower occupational health and workplace safety registration for all employees

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — official portal: www.eta.gov.eg; electronic services platform: https://egypttax.gov.eg (including e-invoicing and e-receipts portals)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must register with the Egyptian Tax Authority upon commencement of business or upon exceeding VAT registration thresholds. Procedure: (1) obtain Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry) certificate and investment license, (2) submit the tax registration application via the ETA e-portal or in-person at the competent tax office, (3) file Charter/Articles of Association, certificate of incorporation, lease or ownership proof of business premises, board resolution appointing the tax representative, and passport/commercial registration copies of non-resident shareholders, (4) obtain the Tax Card (Faith Tax Card) recording the Consolidated Tax Number (TIN), which also serves as the VAT identification number, (5) register for payroll tax (monthly income tax withholding), stamp duty, and WHT registration with the same TIN. The LLC may also obtain a separate customs number (I/C code) from the Egyptian Customs Authority for import/export activity. Registration must be completed within 30 days of incorporation or before commencing taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Egyptian law; an Egyptian LLC is mandatorily taxed at the entity level as a juridical person under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005. Profit distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to withholding tax at source. The only available administrative elections relate to the simplified presumptive tax regime for small businesses (turnover below EGP 10 million, with an irrevocable election for a 3-year period), cash-basis election for certain taxpayers, and tax treaty relief by advance application. Egyptian transfer-pricing rules incorporate hybrid mismatch concepts only via the OECD/G20 Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) minimum standards; no domestic check-the-box hybrid mismatch election is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.exempt_zone_note: The Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) and certain free zones may offer a 0% corporate income tax rate for eligible entities subject to obtaining SCZONE license and advance ETA confirmation; such treatment not automatically available to a standard LLC

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) introduced by Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods and services (mandatory registration); EGP 90,000 threshold for partial registration of exempt persons; voluntary registration permitted below threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt regime administered by the ETA. Taxpayers above the specified turnover threshold (phased implementation; currently mandatory for entities with annual turnover above EGP 50 million) must issue invoices and receipts exclusively through ETA-approved electronic channels. The ETA operates a real-time clearance model (API-based integration with taxpayer ERP systems, SOAP/REST, and fiscal device digital stamping). Each invoice receives an internal registration number and unique QR 2D barcode; documents must be reported to the ETA e-invoicing platform within 24 hours of issuance. Fiscal stamping of cash registers (e-receipts) is mandatory in the retail sector. Non-compliance triggers suspension of VAT refunds and blockage of the taxpayer's digital fiscal identity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated under Article 30 of Law 67/2016 where the goods are transported out of Egypt or the services are performed and consumed wholly outside Egypt, including transport, insurance, and directly related services for exported goods. A revenue-based financing fund providing cross-border royalty or advisory services may claim zero-rating only upon documentary proof that the recipient is a non-resident, the service is not used by an Egyptian establishment, and the fee flows from outside Egypt. Intra-group offshore services with no Egyptian consumption also qualify if the supply qualifies as an 'exported service' under ETA guidance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Bill of Exit (Electronic Customs Clearance System)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign currency bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible currency
Signed export sale contract or proforma invoice
ETA e-invoice with zero-rated supply code
Copy of the registered export registry (export file) maintained by the taxpayer
Proof of deconsolidation of goods at the port of final destination (for re-export scenarios)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may retroactively claw back zero-rated treatment and assess full 14% VAT plus late payment penalties (currently up to 2% per month on the tax due) if export documentation is deficient, goods are diverted to domestic consumption, or export proceeds are not repatriated within the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) 180-day deadline. False zero-rating claims constitute VAT evasion under Law 67/2016 Articles 51-52, punishable by a fine of no less than 100% of the tax due and up to 1000% in case of fraudulent documentation, plus imprisonment of both the legal representative and the foreign entity's local tax agent. The ETA also applies an automatic 1.5x assessment multiplier and criminal referral where fake export receipts or forged inward remittance certificates are detected. For services, the ETA can recharacterize an offshore service as Egyptian-source and disallow the zero-rating if the local fund performs management or financing functions in Egypt or invoices in EGP to a domestic entity. Export VAT refunds are subject to pre-refund audit; the refund may be suspended until the CBE confirms FX repatriation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole monetary authority and foreign-exchange administrator, exercising statutory powers under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020. The CBE licenses all onshore dealer banks, operates the interbank FX market, sets the EGP fixing methodology, and supervises payment infrastructure including RTGS, ACH, and the InstaPay instant-payment network.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt accepted IMF Article VIII (full current-account convertibility) in 1991. The capital account is comparably open: foreign investors registered with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 enjoy unrestricted repatriation of capital, dividends, and loan proceeds through CBE-licensed banks. Following the March 2024 currency-unification decision, the CBE removed the previous prior-approval queues, LC-only import rule, and FX margin caps; banks now execute conversions for any declared underlying transaction, subject to document-based verification. Practical hurdles for profit remittance are limited to (i) submission of audited financial statements and tax-clearance certificates, and (ii) momentary intra-day EGP liquidity tightness, which does not normally trigger a denial.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation or mandatory conversion ratio exists for export proceeds. The former surrender regime rooted in Law No. 38 of 1977 was abolished in the 2003 liberalization package and was not revived by the 2020 banking law. Corporate exporters may retain 100% of export and royalty receipts in onshore foreign-currency accounts or convert them at will; the only foundational requirements are declaration to the receiving bank using the CBE/BPM-6 purpose codes and retention of the underlying contract for five years for the bank's audit trail.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Collection & Settlement Account (EGP) plus USD clearing account
Multi-currency Operational Account (USD/EUR/EGP) with priority cross-border service
Capital Escrow / Capital Injection Account (EGP and USD)
Operational Account and Treasury Hedging Line (EGP)
Operational Account with InstaPay and RTGS connectivity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: MEDIUM. A regulated offshore digital EMI is viable only as a first-mile collection originator, not as a substitute for the onshore bank account. A foreign EMI must be duly licensed in its home jurisdiction (e.g., FCA-authorized UK EMI or EU e-money institution) and may collect ACH and direct-debit payments from digital-brand merchants, subsequently wiring the monthly aggregate to the Egyptian LLC via SWIFT MT103. However, the CBE does not recognize offshore EMIs for the purpose of statutory corporate settlement accounts, EGP clearing, tax evidence, or FX hedging; the LLC must maintain its treasury core with a CBE-licensed bank and ensure that all contractual documentation expressly disclaims deposit-taking activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote account opening without any physical or notarized touchpoint is not accepted in standard CBE AML practice. At least one authorized signatory or senior director must be identified through a face-to-face or officially video-recorded compliance interview with the bank's AML officer. Non-resident directors may avoid travel to Cairo if the corporate resolutions, specimen signatures, and power of attorney for the onshore manager are notarized at the Egyptian Consulate and apostilled where required. In practice, private banks (CIB, HSBC) accept a pre-arranged video interview after receipt of the notarized file, while state-owned banks (NBE, Banque Misr) generally insist on physical presence of the signatory at the branch for the initial account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed non-bank financial-services risk: the ISIC 6499 code, combined with the absence of any CBE or payment license, is initially screened as possible unauthorized deposit-taking or money-service business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An Egyptian legal memorandum classifying the revenue-based financing as a price-assigned purchase of future royalty streams rather than deposits or collective lending; the fund-side capital escrow account held at a CBE-licensed bank; investor agreements expressly disclaiming banking activities; evidence of no public solicitation; and a clear fund-flow diagram showing collection, warehousing, and repayment only to identified investors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through or aggregation red flag: frequent same-month inflow sweeps to foreign investors may trigger suspicion of unlicensed remittance or payment aggregation services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy demonstrating a minimum onshore warehousing period; a matched-assets ledger showing one investor position per revenue stream; full end-recipient UBO identification; and, for volumes above the bank's concentration threshold, a banking-licensed PSP application under Law No. 18 of 2019 filed before the first full month of operation, or alternatively an escrow-agent mandate accepted by the bank's compliance department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-brand and e-commerce counterparties across the MENA and GCC region create elevated adverse-media, sanctions-affinity, and unregulated-payment-acceptor exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-merchant comparator pack comprising corporate extract or sole-trader identification, platform sales history, licensed-PSP attestation, OFAC/EU/UN targeted-sanctions screening output, negative-news search results, and a monthly refreshed client-risk rating; onboarding is denied for any brand that cannot evidence the legitimate source of its receivables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO concentration and seat opacity (100% foreign ownership is legally permitted under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, but banks treat multi-layer offshore holding structures as high-risk).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO file identifying every natural person with a 25% or greater interest, including national ID or passport copies, residential-address proof, home-bank reference letters, and wealth-source supported by audited financial statements; supplemented by the GAFI registration extract and the commercial registration certificate evidencing the directorship chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-trip and synthetic-turnover typology: high-frequency FX conversions and fast EGP/USD churn increase scrutiny as potential circular laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-supported treasury mandate limiting conversions to actual royalty receipts and verified trade obligations; dual-signatory treasury authorization protocol; real-time reconciliation files exported monthly; a five-year retention protocol; and an externally audited financial-reporting pack delivered annually to reduce the bank's compliance burden.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant sequence: (1) the foreign investor remits a SWIFT MT103 from its bank to the LLC's USD Capital Escrow Account at the chosen CBE-licensed bank, quoting the BPM-6 direct-investment purpose code for share capital or equity transactions, with Field 70 references containing the GAFI registration number, the current commercial registration extract, and the board resolution increasing capital; (2) the receiving bank verifies the GAFI no-objection letter and the CBE Capital Declaration, then posts the account; (3) treasury converts only the EGP-denominated liquidity tranche through the interbank market, preserving the USD balance for the royalty fund's capital base; (4) the investor's shareholding and the transferred amount are recorded in the Commercial Registry within the statutory filing period and added to the capital-base evidence monitored by the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EGP-denominated obligations, including royalty payments to Egyptian digital brands and local operating costs, are cleared via CBE RTGS for high-value payments and the InstaPay instant-payment network for micro-settlements, both keyed off the national 29-character IBAN; repeated low-value collections are executed through Direct-Debit ACH mandates under standard clearing rules. Cross-border USD payments to investors, foreign suppliers, and IP royalties are cleared via SWIFT MT103 through the correspondent banking chain, with MT202 COV or MT202 used for bank-to-bank treasury positioning; import-related settlements by clients are structured as irrevocable documentary letters of credit under UCP600 opened by the local bank. EUR and GBP denominations are cleared through the CBE dealer bank's Euro and Sterling nostro chains.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards — onshore interbank product, tenors from 7 days to 12 months, requiring a demonstrable trade or investment underlying
FX Swaps (spot-forward and tom-next) for daily treasury liquidity matching
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) with CBE-licensed dealer banks to hedge long-dated USD/EGP funding mismatches
Vanilla FX Options — available bilaterally with the bank, exercised only against the same underlying-documentation evidence

All instruments must be delivered onshore; offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible in the current Egyptian regime, as access to the EGP is liberalized and the CBE expects hedging to occur in the licensed interbank market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of fiscal year-end; for calendar-year filers, by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 2% of tax due per month or part thereof, up to 100% of the assessed tax; late payment interest accrues; repeated non-filing triggers tax audit, enforced collection, and administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval within six months of fiscal year-end; filing with GAFI and Commercial Registry within 30 days after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file prevents issuance of compliance certificates, renewals, and government clearances; GAFI may levy administrative fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 20,000; two consecutive years of non-filing may result in administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of initial commercial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs daily penalty charges; registration is suspended after 30 days of delinquency; continued non-renewal may lead to deletion from the Commercial Registry after one year of notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Annual Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the registration anniversary and within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance or inaccurate UBO filing is punishable under the Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002; fines up to EGP 200,000 and imprisonment of responsible officers; register may be inspected and struck off for repeated non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs are statutorily required to appoint at least one independent auditor; no small-company exemption applies for a financing fund entity, and audited financial statements are mandatory for registration filings and tax purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), converged with IFRS; financial statements presented in Egyptian Pounds (EGP) unless functional currency authorization is obtained.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A register of beneficial owners must be maintained at the registered office and updated annually on the company's formation anniversary. Any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be reported to GAFI within 30 days. The transfer is only effective and opposable to third parties upon entry in the Register of Members.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket corporate tax holiday. Preferential items include: (i) 0% CIT on export-linked profits of free-zone licensed projects under Investment Law No. 72/2017; (ii) investment cost deduction of up to 50% of eligible capital expenditure for approved strategic or rural projects; (iii) application of the participation exemption to qualifying dividend receipts; (iv) 25% entertainment expense limitation and other sector-specific deductions. A non-dilutive revenue-based financing fund under ISIC 6499 generally does not qualify for export incentives and would be taxed at the headline 22.5% rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: National Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Return – Form No. 19; mandatory electronic filing through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) unified e-Tax electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The LLC must also settle provisional tax instalments during the fiscal year under the ETA instalment schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 4 months from the fiscal year-end. Default fiscal year is the calendar year (deadline: 30 April); a different fiscal year is permitted only with prior ETA approval, and the 4-month rule applies relative to that year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Card Number and registered company name.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the ETA-issued tax card number and the exact legal name in Arabic or English as registered with the commercial register. Non-resident shareholders must be separately disclosed in the nationality/foreign ownership section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, registered head office address, and Egyptian agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert 'Limited Liability Company' and the Egyptian registered address. If the LLC is managed from abroad, provide the address of the Egyptian resident manager or tax representative appointed under Law No. 91/2005.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable period (fiscal year start and end dates).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the period covered by the Egyptian audited financial statements; the foreign parent's fiscal year is not relevant unless an ETA-approved aligned year-end exists.

State ISIC Rev. 4 code 6499 (Other financial service activities) and NAICS 2022 code 525990. The foreign parent must confirm the LLC is not operating as a lender requiring a Central Bank of Egypt license, because revenue-based financing structured as purchases of future revenues is not a banking activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue, including revenue-based financing instalments, royalties, commissions, and any other income from Egyptian and foreign sources.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident LLC is taxed on worldwide income. All amounts received from foreign digital brand counterparties must be included; no territorial apportionment is permitted for the LLC itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses (cost of funds, direct overheads, bad debts, and amortization), subject to tax caps on entertainment, fines, and undocumented costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties (royalties, interest, management fees) are deductible only when supported by written agreements and compliant with the arm's length principle and Egyptian transfer pricing thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit before tax per the audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the financial statements audited by an Egyptian-licensed audit firm. Non-resident investors must ensure the audit opinion covers the full legal-entity fund operation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory additions to accounting profit (non-deductible provisions, deferred tax, excess entertainment, and TP adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party charges not at arm's length, including intra-group financing margins and royalty mark-ups, must be added back unless a valid benchmark study is retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory deductions from accounting profit (tax-exempt income, qualifying dividend participation exemption, investment incentives).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from foreign subsidiaries qualify for the participation exemption only if the holding percentage and holding period conditions are met; documentary evidence must be filed with the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after additions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The amount must reconcile completely with the related-party disclosure (Form No. 80 TP annex). Any inconsistency between the return and the commercial invoices issued to foreign digital brands triggers an ETA audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax due at 22.5% on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard rate only; free-zone or branch profits require separate rate codes. Revenue-based financing funds have no statutory rate reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and prepayments: provisional instalments, foreign tax credits, and prior-year prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require certified foreign tax assessments and a tax residency certificate. No credit is granted for taxes paid by the foreign parent or shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure and transfer pricing annex (Form No. 80).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Itemize every cross-border controlled transaction by type (royalty, financing, receivables purchase), amount, and country. Failure to attach this annex renders the entire filing incomplete.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration signed by the authorized legal representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident director or general manager must sign jointly with the Egyptian tax agent. The signatory assumes personal criminal liability for the accuracy of the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing: fine of EGP 500 to EGP 5,000. Unpaid tax accrues delay interest at 2% per month (capped at 100% of the tax). Inaccurate or incomplete returns cause reassessment, additional tax, fines from 100% to 200% of evaded tax, blacklisting, enforced bank attachment, and travel bans against authorized signatories.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on distributions of profits to all shareholders (Article 56, Law No. 91/2005). The withholding is a final tax for resident and non-resident individuals and is creditable or refundable for corporate shareholders according to their domestic law.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To reduce the 10% statutory WHT under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA): (1) the non-resident shareholder obtains an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority for the calendar year; (2) the shareholder submits to the Egyptian paying LLC a treaty relief application containing a declaration of beneficial ownership, shareholding evidence, and confirmation of economic substance (board minutes, premises, personnel); (3) the application file is lodged with the Egyptian Tax Authority through the e-Tax portal together with the certified TRC and audited documentation; (4) only after ETA approval may the LLC withhold at the treaty rate (typically 5% for holdings of 10% or more and 10% for portfolio investments); otherwise the 10% statutory WHT is withheld and a refund claim may be filed with the ETA within 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding rate of 20%; treaty rates are commonly reduced to 10% to 20%, with technical-service royalties often at 10% to 15%. Interest: statutory withholding rate of 20%; treaty reductions are typically 10% to 15%; interest on foreign loans approved by the Central Bank of Egypt may be exempt from Egyptian WHT under specific ministerial rules. Both payments require arm's length pricing, beneficial ownership proof, and compliance with Egyptian thin-capitalization and general anti-avoidance provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where annual controlled transactions with related parties exceed EGP 8,000,000. Master File: mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds EGP 200,000,000. Country-by-Country Report: mandatory where group consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 15,000,000,000, subject to the Egyptian Tax Authority notification deadlines.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute, but economic substance is enforced through four horizontal pillars: (i) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Art. 106, Law No. 91/2005) allows the ETA to disregard transactions or arrangements lacking a valid commercial purpose or business substance; (ii) the Egyptian TP Guidelines require a complete functional, asset, and risk (FAR) analysis such that a royalty/financing fund LLC without employees, premises, and local decision-making in Egypt is treated as a pure conduit; (iii) the beneficial ownership doctrine under DTAs denies treaty relief on payments to bare-shell recipients; (iv) the AML Law No. 80/2002 obliges identification of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of the fund. An Egyptian LLC acting solely as a pass-through financing vehicle will therefore be recharacterized and taxed on an arm's length basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting revenue-based financing income, royalties, or interest from Form No. 19; fabricating deductions; issuing forged invoices; or submitting a false transfer pricing disclosure to suppress Egyptian corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 133 of Law No. 91/2005: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a fine equal to 100% to 200% of the tax evaded; additional assessment, delay interest at 2% per month (capped at 100%), taxpayer blacklisting, and forced collection by bank attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the erroneous return are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, delay surcharges, and fines. They face criminal imprisonment, civil restitution from personal assets, and an administrative travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a zero-employee, no-office Egyptian LLC used solely to route royalty and financing flows to claim DTA benefits that the ultimate beneficial owner could not obtain directly under Limitation-on-Benefits or beneficial ownership clauses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA denies treaty relief and applies the full statutory WHT (20% on royalties and interest); the arrangement is recharacterized under the GAAR (Art. 106), thin-capitalization rules reclassify the debt, and fines and delay interest are imposed on the entire adjusted amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and authorized signatories are exposed to civil restitution, travel bans, and personal liability for uncollected withholding tax. The foreign ultimate beneficial owner may be deemed resident in Egypt and assessed personally for the avoided corporate tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to attach the Form No. 80 transfer pricing disclosure to the CIT return; failing to prepare or maintain the Local File or Master File when the statutory thresholds are exceeded; executing royalty or financing agreements with no benchmark analysis or comparability study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of up to EGP 100,000; the return is treated as incomplete; the ETA makes a mandatory upward adjustment to the arm's length price, with delay interest at 2% per month up to 100% of the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The signing director is personally liable for the transfer pricing adjustment, penalties, and surcharges. In cases of intentional mispricing, criminal tax evasion charges and a travel ban apply to the responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC deducts the 10% dividend WHT or the 20% royalty/interest WHT from a non-resident payee but fails to remit the withheld amounts to the Egyptian Tax Authority within the prescribed deadlines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate demand for the unremitted WHT plus delay interest at 2% per month (capped at 100%); administrative fine of up to EGP 20,000; enforcement by attachment of bank accounts; refusal to issue the company's tax clearance certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted withholding tax, and statutory collection tools include seizure of personal assets and a travel ban against the responsible directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Revenue-Based Financing LLC to collect high-volume ACH and wire transfer receipts from foreign digital brands without maintaining enhanced KYC/UBO verification, suspicious transaction reporting, or an AML compliance program required for a medium-risk financial vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Egyptian AML Law No. 80/2002 (as amended): imprisonment of 2 to 7 years and a fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000; freezing of accounts; administrative sanctions including license revocation or closure of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers knowingly involved in money laundering are criminally liable, subject to civil confiscation of laundered assets, and face international and domestic travel bans.
